While the news of Robert Pattinson 's casting as the new James Bond has sparked a frenzy on social media, Léa Seydoux, who starred opposite Daniel Craig in two James Bond movies, has little interest in finding out who will play the next Bond girl.

Speaking on a recent episode of The Runthrough podcast which was recorded before Pattinson was announced as the new OO7, Seydoux was asked who she thought should play the next Bond girl, or Bond woman. “I don’t really care,” she said, laughing. “I don’t really care, guys. “It became American. But I’m sure the movie will be great because it’s directed by Denis Villeneuve , who’s a very talented director. I’m sure he will do something great,” she said.

articles.title: 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth' Review: Brad Pitt Hits the Aura Jackpot in a Very Fun Tarantino Hangout Movie That Feels Like QT TV
articles.summary: "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" gives you a highly pleasurable, shaggy heat-of-the-moment buzz. I’m not sure what I was expecting from a sequel to "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," but I dug just about every ambling, low-down minute of this one.
articles.content:
" The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth " gives you a highly pleasurable, shaggy heat-of-the-moment buzz. I’m not sure what I was expecting from a sequel to "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," but I dug just about every ambling, low-down minute of this one. (I realize that low-down is an ancient phrase, but this is a movie that ends with Boz Scaggs' "Lowdown" playing over the closing credits. That’s how 1977 it is.)

The film is Quentin Tarantino , who wrote the screenplay, going wherever the day (or night) takes him. And that will do just fine. But it’s also Tarantino honed and manicured, given a polish of precision by the film’s director, David Fincher . As an artist, the hot-blooded, motormouth Tarantino is Dionysian; the rigorously controlled, ice-in-his-veins Fincher is Apollonian. Together, the two merge in a divertingly odd way. "The Further Mis-Adventures" is an enjoyable contradiction — a meticulous hangout movie. It hops from one thing to the next, but it's disarmingly placid and even-keeled about what it’s doing. In spirit, it’s almost as if someone had slipped the movie half a Quaalude. It’s got no worries, and neither does its hero, Cliff Booth ( Brad Pitt ), the most sexy-cool aging ex-stuntman you’ll ever see. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Queen Latifah, Bone Thugs-N-Harmony, MC Lyte and More to Lead 2027 Rock the Bells Cruise

"The Further Mis-Adventures" sprawls over one week in Los Angeles in the latter half of '77 (the specificity has meaning; it’s supposed to be just after "Star Wars" has changed the force of the movie universe), and the tone is less sunlit intense than the 1969 of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood." The counterculture has now evaporated, and everyone is stuck in a lackadaisical limbo of diversion, with one foot in the past. That doesn’t mean "The Further Mis-Adventures" is snobbish about the pop-culture era it’s rooted in. The film is brazenly and ever-so-slightly-ironically approving, whether it’s reveling in the throb of disco or the grand orchestral pomp of ELO’s "Tightrope," smacking its lips at a tacky margarita bar that features mud-wrestling night, or opening with a last-days-of-blaxploitation movie called "Soul Brothers Die Hard!," in which a couple of mack daddies sit around talking about the libidinous challenge of keeping their stables happy. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

There’s a trick that Tarantino and Fincher spring several times here, and that’s to lure us into a piece of entertainment — a movie, a TV show — as if it were actually happening. That’s their tribute to the canny power of this stuff. Yet even as "The Further Mis-Adventures" embraces all this, you can feel a certain what’s-next? affectlessness hanging in the smoggy air. The only one who doesn’t feel it is Cliff, who lives in the eternal present. You might say that Cliff has become something of a loser. His old buddy Rick Dalton, who kept him supplied with stunt-double work, is now history (Rick has moved to Australia), and Cliff, with a slight limp and aching joints, is a man pushing 50, living with his cranky pawn-shop-owner dad (Peter Weller) in Marina del Rey, working odd jobs, driving around in his muscle-car jalopy. Yet in his slightly grizzled way he’s still a dreamboat, not to mention the most comfortable man in his own skin God ever invented.

Bringing Cliff back and expanding him into a more central presence, Brad Pitt hits the aura jackpot. With a Redford mustache and killer grin and golden sweep of honey-blond hair, parading around in gaudy short-sleeve bartender shirts with three or four buttons open, he makes Cliff high on his own supply of flinty good vibes. Cliff takes whatever comes at him, and that’s a life that suits him fine. He’s chivalrous and polite, but that’s connected to how comfortable he is with violence. He has no anxiety about it, and no anxiety about anything else. Pitt takes his own slightly seedy movie-star nobility and turns it up to full irresistible throttle. Even his voice is yummy — the sandy baritone directness of it, with that hint of a SoCal drawl. His Cliff puts everyone at ease, including the audience, but he keeps you guessing because he’s a paradox: a himbo with brains who can read anyone in the room — a sexy cowboy handyman who, if need be, will cut your throat.

The film’s opening episode is an appetizer of violence. It’s Tuesday night, and Cliff is working his shift as a projectionist at the New Beverly Cinema (the first of the film’s Tarantino Easter-egg in-jokes — there will be more, including a TV commercial for Red Apple cigarettes featuring Margot Robbie’s Sharon Tate). The theater is showing "Soul Brothers Die Hard!," and Cliff talks along with some of the tastier dialogue as he changes reels. But his real job comes after the theater closes. That’s when he has to rendezvous with a scurvy thief (Karren Karagulian), who has brought along the twink hustler (Corey Fogelmanis) he picked up on Santa Monica Boulevard. The thief is looking to fence some items he stole from a house in the Hollywood Hills. But the robbery victim, unbeknownst to him, is one of Cliff’s old director pals. In short order, Cliff gets rid of the thief and puts the hustler on a bus back to Ohio. The shock — and joke — of it is that Cliff kills a man as casually as if he were mixing a banana margarita on his bartending night. That’s the Zen of Cliff Booth. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Fincher has referred to "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" as "'Shampoo' with violence" (an ace description), and that’s to say: It’s all about Cliff drifting around. It isn't necessarily trying to be a movie story. But the film is fixated on Hollywood, to the point that each new location is identified with an onscreen title that will say (for instance) "Beverly Hills, 4.3 miles west of Hollywood," as if Hollywood were the nucleus of the universe. What’s telling about "Cliff Booth" is that in its random anecdotal hangout way, it’s actually rooted in the world of television.

Rick moved to Australia because he’s starring in a TV series there called "Dingo Dan." Those items stolen by the thief include a best director Oscar statuette, which implies that that trophy is a relic of a lost age. And the plot of "The Further Mis-Adventures" centers on Cliff getting summoned by Charlie Peters ( Scott Caan ), a garishly obnoxious star of TV Westerns and combat series. Charlie, who thinks he knows everything, does all his own stunt work (which suggests the character might be a Tarantino tweak of Tom Cruise — though the two characters, aside from being of average height, don’t have much else in common). Charlie, though, needs Cliff for something else: to get him out of an underworld jam. This is, after all, the stuntman who beat up Bruce Lee.

So Cliff meets with Charlie’s agent, the imperially tall, British, and coldly sexy Kate Crosby ( Elizabeth Debicki ). These two get a flirtation going — one so frosty that in spirit it feels more 2026 than 1977. You can see that there’s a mutual attraction. And you really see it after Cliff confesses his feelings, and their gamesmanship turns weirdly kinky. (The weird part is that the kink stays so casual.) But she’s classy and standoffish, and the most revealing conversation the two have is about the movies.

It’s one of those freewheeling Tarantino digressions (built on what sounds like a scrap from his abandoned script for "The Critic"), in which Kate tells Cliff that she was briefly a film critic who had gotten to know Pauline Kael (who Cliff dismisses because she didn’t like "Butch Cassidy"). Kate, sounding like a corrupt studio executive, says she now thinks of movies strictly as entertainment, and never as art. Cliff asks: Even "The Godfather"? Yes, she says, that’s just a gangster movie with artistic airs. It’s strange that the film never counters this view; it's almost as if Tarantino agrees with it. Has he gone that far into pulp fetishization? (The author of "Cinema Speculation" is actually a great critic.) Or maybe he's saying: Now that "Star Wars" has arrived, the movies as we knew them are dead. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I’m going on about this because I think it helps explain the enjoyably random, slightly disjunctive air of "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth." It’s the first Tarantino film that feels, in its structural DNA, like a glorified television series. At one point, the movie was supposed to be a series, and in spirit that’s kind of what it still is. Call it QT TV. The incidents hook you, but with less consequence than they’d have in a full-blown, let-it-rip Tarantino movie. "The Further Mis-Adventures" looks like a movie (Fincher gives it a stately sheen), and it’s way too violent for television. But the hangout factor, in this case, feels one small step removed from the characters-on-a-TV-series-are-your-family factor.

Driving the action forward are a pair of Filipino hitmen, the Verdusco brothers (Matt Groove and JB Tadena), who are singular in their viciousness; one employs a scary hatchet he calls Esmerelda. Scott Caan does a blustery job of playing Charlie, the blowhard TV star (I enjoyed the scene where he uses a live round of ammunition to put the fear into Timothy Olyphant as a fellow actor playing a Nazi), but given how central the character is, I wish he were less of a putz. I also wish we didn’t have to watch Roderick "Hot Rod" Harrison (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II), Charlie’s football-player-turned-actor costar, get not simply beat up but maimed for no good reason. On the other hand, I appreciated the quick reference to Cliff doing porn, which becomes a punchline to the fact that everyone he meets feels like they’ve seen him before. Speaking of porn, there’s a shoutout/tweak to PTA when "Best of My Love," the Emotions track that opens "Boogie Nights," comes on the car radio and Cliff flips the channel.

How is the ultraviolent climax? It’s kind of spectacular. Tarantino doesn’t use it to rewrite history this time, but in a funny way he does an instant mini version of that. What happens to Cliff in the big fight at the end should, by all rights, have eliminated him from the earth. But it doesn’t. It’s just a scratch. He doesn’t give a fuck, and he’s still there. To put it in QT TV terms: When’s the next episode?

articles.title: ‘The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth’ Review: The Vibes Are Off In David Fincher’s Dark, Dank, Grubby Tarantino Episode
articles.summary: There’s a strong argument to be made that if you’ve read Quentin Tarantino ’s “ Once Upon A Time In Hollywood ” novelization, “ The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth ” shouldn’t surprise you. Tarantino’s book was shaggy and baggy, like an unedited, freehand version of the movie, full of detours, tangents, and narrative cul-de-sacs. An interesting extended curiosity, mildly entertaining in spots, but much of it probably wouldn’t have stood on its own outside the pulp novel format. EXCLUSIVE: Comedian Gabriel "Fluffy" Iglesias has hit on a major milestone with Lone Star Fluffy , a new hour special marking his fifth for Netflix and 10th overall.

Directed by Manny Rodriguez, the special premieres globally on December 24.

From biker bars to sold-out stadiums, Iglesias has spent 30 years turning life's chaos into laughs. His new special brings his storytelling to Texas, taking on Lone Star rivalries, family antics and wild run-ins with a comedy legend and a pop superstar.

Produced by Fluffy Shop Studios and Triage Entertainment, the special was shot at The Tobin Center for the Performing Arts in San Antonio, Texas. Iglesias, John Bravakis and Joe Meloche served as executive producers. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Casting 'The Watcher': Luke David Blumm Returns, Veronica Dunne Among Quartet Joining Season 2 Cast Casting 'Bridgerton' Star Hannah Dodd Joins Nick Jonas In Netflix Holiday Rom-Com 'The More The Merrier'

The first, Gabriel Iglesias : Legend of Fluffy , hit the streamer's global most watched list, ranking as its third most-watched special of 2025. Ranking among the highest grossing touring comedians of all time, Iglesias is one of the few to achieve the hat trick of headlining and selling out Madison Square Garden in New York, Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and The Sydney Opera House in Australia. The fourth highest grossing comedian of 2025 according to Billboard , he continues to make the Top 10 year after year.

Iglesias is also one of the most watched comedians on YouTube with over 2.7 billion views and over 35.9 million fans across social media. In 2022, he made history as the first comedian to perform at and sell out Dodger Stadium, and earlier this year, he co-headlined the first-ever stand-up show at SoFi Stadium, alongside Jo Koy.

Iglesias is also known for starring in and exec producing the Netflix sitcom Mr. Iglesias , which ran for three seasons. articles.title: A “Very Human” Father-Daughter Story: ‘THR Presents’ Q&A With Myrsini Aristidou on Cyprus’ First Oscar Submission, ‘Hold Onto Me’
articles.summary: The director of Sundance audience winner on casting a first-time actress, shooting a night scene in a freezing sea and her films’ love stories.
articles.content:
Cyprus has submitted its first-ever international feature film Oscar contender:  Hold Onto Me , the feature debut of writer-director Myrsini Aristidou.

The film, starring newcomer Maria Petrova and Christos Passalis ( Dogtooth ), premiered at Sundance, where it won the World Cinema Dramatic Audience Award. It follows Iris, 11, whose grandfather has died, which leads to petty criminal Aris — the father she has never known — arriving in town. Can what starts out as a stubborn attempt to connect develop into a fragile bond? Related Stories Movies The Free World Award Is Made From Weapons Metal. The First Winner: Iraq's Oscar Entry Movies "Hollywood Rewrites History" and Calls for Authentic Female Characters: Tallinn Debates Cinema Amid Global Crisis

Hold Onto Me is a Cyprus-Denmark-Greece co-production that takes a deep dive into a beach community and is partially inspired by the filmmaker's personal experience. During a taping of THR Presents , Aristidou shared how "the narrative arc of all my films is sort of a love story and the disappointments that come with it." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Hold Onto Me is based in Cyprus, but addresses universal themes. How would you describe what the film explores? And how important was it for you to show us characters who are not fully good or bad?

The subject matter is something that I care about a lot — all of us [do], I think. Our relationship with our parents matters. It is something we carry with us. We either work on it to improve it or make it better or heal it — or many people let it go as well and just move on and try not to repeat the same patterns. …

I care a lot about characters that are real, that are very imperfect, very human in their own way, and maybe even lonely in many ways.

How did you cast young Maria as Iris?

She had never done acting before, actually. Our casting director found her in Cyprus. She was younger than what I had written in the script. I wrote the script for a 15-year-old, and she was 10 and a half at the time. Yet, there was something about her. There was this innocence and authenticity. There is an emergency scene in the sea. I don't imagine you had a big water tank that you filmed in? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It was very, very different and complicated. We didn't have the budget to shoot in a pool. We shot in the sea. It was very cold; we shot at night. … We were splashing water with our hands.

articles.title: It Girl India Amarteifo’s Queen’s Gambit
articles.summary: The 25-year-old actress followed her 'Bridgerton' breakthrough with a long, thoughtful pause. Now she’s making her move with ‘Clarissa.’
articles.content:
India Amarteifio went to bed on May 3, 2023, a working but largely unknown young actress. The next morning — after Netflix dropped Queen Charlotte : A Bridgerton Story , a prequel in which Amarteifio plays a younger version of Golda Rosheuvel's imperious royal — she woke up famous.

"The first thing I did that day was walk down the street with my co-star Corey [Mylchreest], and we were immediately recognized and stopped by fans," she says. "We just looked at each other like, 'OK, life has changed now.' "

Three years later, Amarteifio, 25, is still getting stopped on the street — at least three or four times a day. "People still rewatch it, or a new Bridgerton comes out and puts the spotlight back on," she says. "I do wonder whether I'm going to be Queen Charlotte forever." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies A "Very Human" Father-Daughter Story: 'THR Presents' Q&A With Myrsini Aristidou on Cyprus' First Oscar Submission, 'Hold Onto Me' Movies The Free World Award Is Made From Weapons Metal. The First Winner: Iraq's Oscar Entry

Not a bad problem to have, considering her previous career anxiety: that her days as an actor might already be finished.

Amarteifio grew up in Southwest London, where acting classes helped burn off excess energy ("I was quite a bouncy child"). Her mother, a beautician, spotted newspaper advertisements for West End casting calls, leading to roles in The Lion King and Matilda , the latter an experience she likens to military training. She picked up representation and television work, including an episode of Sex Education , but graduated from drama school straight into the pandemic.

"It's so silly, but I wasn't booking anything, and I thought, 'My time has passed at 20 years old,' " she says with a laugh.

Then came Queen Charlotte — and literal overnight success. The series instantly hit No. 1 on Netflix, topped Nielsen's streaming charts and went on to surpass 80 million views, becoming one of the platform's most popular titles. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

After waiting so long for her big break, Amarteifio was willing to wait a little longer for the right follow-up. She took a long pause after Queen Charlotte , thinking about the career she wanted beyond the show that had made her famous. The offers were coming, but she was holding out for "more art house, indie, character-driven" projects.

She found what she was looking for in Clarissa , a Neon film from Nigerian twin filmmakers Arie and Chuko Esiri that opens in select U.S. theaters Dec. 11. Their reimagining of Mrs. Dalloway casts Hotel Rwanda Oscar nominee Sophie Okonedo as a Lagos society woman revisiting the summer that shaped her life, with Amarteifio taking over in the flashbacks. Ayo Edebiri and David Oyelowo round out the cast.

Cast and crew lived communally at the Esiris' family resort in Nigeria, canoeing to work daily. "You would look down at the turquoise of the water and look up to see monkeys jumping overhead, and it was unreal," recalls Amarteifio.

She also relished the chance to talk shop with her castmates. "I'm always just like, 'Are you guys OK?' " she says with a laugh. "This industry can be so much sometimes, so I'm really interested in how people are doing and how they look after themselves. And, of course, I look at someone like Ayo and her trajectory and hope my career takes a similar form."

The film's festival run, beginning at Cannes and taking her to Telluride, Toronto and New York, has brought her closer to the kind of attention she wants. Monarch Media has secured the rights to the Jane Hawk books by Dean Koontz with plans to develop them into a TV series, Variety has learned exclusively.

The search is now on for a showrunner to helm the project before it is taken out to market. Koontz is an executive producer along with Monarch Media's Steve Barnett, Alan Powell and Vicky Patel.

“I’m a huge Dean Koontz fan, and like millions of fans of suspense readers, couldn’t wait for the next ‘Jane Hawk’ novel to come out,” said Patel. “I’m so excited to partner my love of Dean’s series with Monarch resources to create what I believe will be a compelling global hit series.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Queen Latifah, Bone Thugs-N-Harmony, MC Lyte and More to Lead 2027 Rock the Bells Cruise

As the books begin, Hawk is a former FBI agent and recent widow seeking answers about the death of her husband, leading her into a high-stakes conspiracy.

“Jane Hawk is a character as dear to me as if she were a real person in my life,” said Koontz. “I am therefore totally delighted that her story is in the hands of such an able and talented team as Steve Barnett, Alan Powell, and Vicky Patel at Monarch.”

The first Jane Hawk book, "The Silent Corner," was published by Penguin Random House in 2017. Four more books in the series have followed: "The Whispering Room" (2017), "The Crooked Staircase" (2018), "The Forbidden Door" (2019), and "The Night Window" (2020). There was previously an attempt to develop Jane Hawk for TV by Paramount Television and Anonymous Content back in 2017, but the project did not move forward.

Koontz has sold over 500 million copies of his books worldwide and has been translated into 38 languages. He has hit number one on the New York Times hardcover bestseller list 14 times in his career, while 16 of his paperback books have gone number one. Koontz is repped by InkWell Management, Cheng Caplan Company, and Frankfurt Kurnit Klein & Selz.

Monarch Media previously produced the hit Richard Linklater film "Hit Man" starring Glen Powell, which debuted at the Venice Film Festival and then in theaters and on Netflix in 2023. The company is also behind the adult animated film "Tangles" starring Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Seth Rogen and Bryan Cranston, which recently premiered at the Cannes Film Festival. News of the new attempt at the Jane Hawk series comes as shows based on book characters with multiple novels to their name are more popular than ever. Just a few similar examples include "Reacher" and "Scarpetta" at Amazon, "The Lincoln Lawyer" at Netflix, and "Will Trent" at ABC.

articles.title: 'The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth' Review: Pitt, Fincher, And Tarantino Team Up For A Rollicking Good Wild Ride Of A 'Hollywood' Follow-Up
articles.summary: Whenever people ask me what my favorite movie of all time is I always have a hard time answering that impossible question, but if you want to know my favorite of the past ten years or so it's simply. I can easily say Quentin Tarantino's 2019 Once Upon A Time In Hollywood. So any idea […]
articles.content:
Whenever people ask me what my favorite movie of all time is I always have a hard time answering that impossible question, but if you want to know my favorite of the past ten years or so it's simply. I can easily say Quentin Tarantino 's 2019 Once Upon A Time In Hollywood.

So any idea of a sequel to this L.A. masterpiece set in 1969 that starred Leonardo DiCaprio and Brad Pitt as Rick Dalton, a movie star who has seen better days, and Cliff Booth his stunt man/sidekick has big shoes to fill following a movie that received 10 Oscar nominations and won 2 including Best Supporting Actor for Pitt. In my opinion it should also have won Best Picture and Director and Tarantino but I digress. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Brad Pitt Backs Robert Pattinson As 007 & Jokingly Pitches Himself As Bond Villain: "I'd Like To Do That" Casting Brad Pitt To Star In 'Connector' From Apple And 'Sound Of Metal' Director Darius Marder

Now with The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth we have one, or should I say "follow-up" since the filmmakers insist this is not a sequel but rather a continuation of the story of Booth set 8 years later in 1977 Hollywood, a bit of a darker time for Cliff and the town, at least in the world according to Q.T. Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

This is the script Tarantino had written for a planned 10th and final directorial film but later scrapped for personal reasons. Pitt however didn't want to let Cliff Booth go and enlisted David Fincher ,his director of Seven, Fight Club, and The Curious Case Of Benjamin Button to take it on, with Tarantino's endorsement of course. Thus arguably the three most exciting filmmakers of their generation (they were all born within a year between 1962 and 1963) have teamed for a hell of an entertaining movie that delivers on every level an uber-fan of Once Upon A Time In Hollywood might expect - and then some - but these 'mis-adventures' are a whole new bag with a brand new set of characters surrounding Booth.

Now it is the summer of '77, a long time since Booth dispatched the members of the Manson clan in Tarantino's parallel history of those real-life horrifying murders in his fairy tale of Hollywood circa '69. Rick Dalton has moved on to Australia and a TV series. Booth is now working as a projectionist at the New Beverly Cinema (the theatre Tarantino owns) and a part-time bartender at Lucy's El Adobe restaurant across the street from Paramount in Hollywood. His other talents, displayed in disposing that tribe of hippies, as well as knocking out Bruce Lee, made him a bit of legendary lore in the town, a past he doesn't really talk about much now but those talents will come in handy again. Just wait. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Booth, still wearing those signature Hawaiian shirts, is a good son who often stops by to watch The Rockford Files and other TV shows with his elderly father, Gus ( Peter Weller ) who also runs a pawn shop and is a bit of a pistol himself. We know however from events at the theatre that start this follow-up that Cliff is also involved with some small time crime as the two thugs he employed to rob an Oscar winning director turn up with the loot and want their money. It's complicated but Cliff is also a fixer who is capable of some pretty violent acts of his own. Say no more but it is an intriuging set up for what is to come.

The main event arrives when he gets a call from a talent agent named Karen Crosby ( Elizabeth Debicki ) on behalf of her client, a big TV star named Charlie Peters ( Scott Caan ), but this is a guy known for doing his own stunts so why does he need Cliff? Nevertheless Cliff's unique talents can serve as strong advice which he gives to Charlie whose own world is as shady as it comes and involves his wife Toni (Carla Gugino) who as it turns out had a romantic laiason with Cliff years earlier. There is also football great turned movie star Roderick 'Hot Rod' Harrison (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II) , and most imposing, the terrifying Filipino Verdusco brothers (Matt Groove and JB Tadena), gangsters who are running around town causing violent chaos with a sledge hammer and some unfinished business for their own "clients" including Peters . Suffice to say all of these characters serve as a set up for a brusing crime story as familiar to Fincher fans as it might be to Tarantino's. This tasty cinematic cocktail is explosive.

If you wonder how this merger of Fincher and Tarantino will work, take comfort in the fact it is a shotgun marriage that fires on all cylinders, a dazzling display of directorial and writing talent unmatched in this genre that create a movie unlike any other out there, and that includes the remarkable one that birthed it.

Pitt clearly knew this role was one he couldn't easily let go of, even when Tarantino decided to deep six the script that would bring him back. Cliff Booth is such a mysterious, laid back guy, capable of anything but never showing his cards. The darker world we now find him inhabiting is startling but the essence of what he was once upon a time in another Hollywood is still there, just ramped up a bit to fit the changing times, and when the occasion arises he also knows how to dress for it. There is more in his closet, literally and figuritively, than those patented shirts. You can see why he won that supporting Oscar (and there is a very funny bit involving one of those during the opening scenes here), but now Pitt's Booth has the starring role and he is a screen character for the ages.

Surrounding him here is a sterling set of actors including the wonderful Debicki playing a woman whose own past is slowly revealed, and who also becomes, against all odds, a romantic interest for Booth in a relationship that is played out in a series of song dedications on local radio station KRLA, a pure Tarantino touch. Caan really gets a showcase here as the fast-talking TV star in a bit over his head. He is simply terrific, as is Weller who has never been better, a real re-discovery of an actor who inhabits the role of Booth's dad with wise wit and warmth. The relationship here between father and son grounds the film in a very smart way, showing a human side of Cliff that balances the darker edges of this scenario perfectly. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

Props also to Gugino who is very fine balancing her rocky marriage to Charlie while also dealing with the emergence of her own past with Cliff. Abdul-Mateen II is ideal casting as a Jim Brown type who will figure into all this mayhem. In fact we first meet him right at the start in a Tarantino specialty, a scene with an unbilled Samuel L. Jackson that turns out to be the blackploitation movie Cliff is running at this theatre. Timothy Olyphant also has a delicious cameo as actor James Stacy. And then there are the Verducso brothers played to the evil hilt by Groove and Tadena who both make about as gruesome a pair you will ever encounter. Welcome to hard times.

The script is full of easter eggs and wry movie and tv references, a pop culture bible of the time that only Tarantino and his brilliant wordsmithing could cook up, and though I am loathe to say he tops himself here, I will say this screenplay matches our expectations in every way. The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth is vintage Tarantino and we are indebted to Fincher for delivering it in style. The director sharply shows off his own unique talents in a movie that never slows down, even with the signature QT monologues, or the fantastic Tarantino-narrated documentary on the career of Charlie Peters. There is so much here this movie will require more than one viewing, that's for sure.

Production wise it is all top of the game across the board including many who have worked with Fincher numerous times including Kirk Baxter's complex editing, Erik Messerschmidt's stunning cinematography, Ren Klyce's complex sound design, Trish Summerville's right-on 70's costume design, and the pitch perfect production design of Donald Graham Burt. The score from Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross also hits the bullseye blending with the songs roaring through the ace soundtrack. And shout out to all the real stunt men employed. The finale is a real corker.

Fincher, Tarantino, and Pitt have hit another one straight out of the park.

Producers are Ceán Chaffin and Pitt.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google While Pokemon Winds and Waves are scheduled for release in 2027 on the Nintendo Switch 2, new leaks like this give fans an early look at what to expect. The latest leaks from the Pokemon Teraleak show a possible new riding feature, a glimpse of the battle gimmick, and the battle style. Game Freak is continually experimenting with features across the series, but these new details seem to indicate the studio is combining aspects from across the mainline and spin-off games to create a completely new hybrid system.

One of the most interesting details concerns how players will explore the world. Riding Pokemon has become increasingly important to the series, and we are constantly seeing new ways this is implemented. We allegedly know that Game Freak wanted all Pokemon to be rideable as opposed to a select few Pokemon, so this leak is a huge development there. Additionally, Pokemon Winds and Waves is reportedly using a new battle gimmick as opposed to bringing back a pre-existing one, like Pokemon Legends: Z-A and Pokemon Champions have done with Mega Evolution.

According to the leaked information , the Rotom Scooter allows players to use their Pokemon's abilities to navigate the environment. Rather than physically riding a Pokemon, Rotom reportedly creates a glowing leash connecting the player to their chosen companion, allowing the player to physically control the Pokemon. The scooter will then change form based on the Pokemon. With this implementation, players should theoretically be able to use any Pokemon as a riding companion.

Combat is another area where Pokemon Winds and Waves could introduce significant changes . The leaked battle system reportedly draws heavily from Pokemon Legends: Arceus , including wild Pokemon being able to attack players directly. Battles will remain turn-based with traditional abilities and other mainline mechanics. The leak also suggests Strong and Agile styles will be absent in Winds and Waves .

The biggest development in battles is the leaked Netsu mechanic, though the name may not be official or stick. Alleged leaked footage shows Blastoise going through the transformation, though exactly what it does is unclear. Reports say that it revolves around weather conditions and may grant Pokemon additional resistances or powerful area-of-effect attacks, which could help with wild Pokemon joining encounters.

Still, these details remain unverified, and development plans can change before release. Whether the Rotom Scooter and Netsu survive into the finished games remains to be seen. With any leak of this nature, it is best to remain skeptical until Game Freak or The Pokemon Company confirms it. That said, these do sound like worthwhile additions to the series and would show off the power of the Nintendo Switch 2.

Doctor Doom looks like he's going to be a wildly powerful antagonist, and there have been some fan concerns about Thor surviving Doomsday . We'll have to see what happens when the movie arrives next month, but the fact that Chris Hemsworth is looking so yoked might be a source of hope for folks who aren't ready to say goodbye to the God of Thunder.

EXCLUSIVE : Kyle Greenberg , longtime head of marketing and distribution at Utopia , is departing the company to launch a consulting startup called Greenhouse .

His new venture plans to develop highly curated, hands-on release strategies for filmmakers, artists, labels and brands to support their own efforts in self-distribution, something an increasing number of producers are turning to given challenges in the current indie film landscape.

Utopia was co-founded by Robert Schwartzman and Cole Harper in 2018. articles.title: I Think I Should Have Seen That Bond Casting Coming When Slow Horses Dropped Its Renewal Announcement
articles.summary: It was staring me right in the face!
articles.content:
Last Monday morning was an exciting time for fans of British spy thrillers. First, Slow Horses was renewed for Seasons 9 and 10, meaning we’ll be getting at least four more seasons of the hit show, available with an Apple TV subscription . Then, just hours later, Amazon MGM finally dropped the bomb we've all been waiting for and announced that the next actor to play James Bond would be Robert Pattinson . Many of us had been waiting for that for months. Years, even, yet it still came as a surprise, given the latest rumors. In hindsight, I probably should have been clued in that the announcement was imminent after the Slow Horses news dropped.

Over the last few weeks and months, there have been a ton of rumors regarding the next Bond ahead of the long-awaited Bond 26 finally beginning production (we’re still not sure when that will actually happen). Names like Jacob Elordi, Henry Cavill , Callum Turner, and more have been rumored. Slow Horses star Jack Lowden was also heavily rumored in recent weeks. Lowden, who plays River Cartwright on the show about disgraced MI5 agents, was looking to make the jump to MI6 and become the ninth man to play Bond .

It’s certainly possible for an actor to appear in multiple projects, but given Slow Horses ' aggressive filming schedule (they have already wrapped Season 7, due next year, and are filming Season 8), it might have been a tough schedule to work out for Lowden had he been named Bond. When the next two seasons were announced, it should have clued me in that Lowden likely wasn’t going to be James Bond going forward. It’s quite possible that Apple may have actually been waiting on the Bond decision to announce it was moving forward with more seasons of Slow Horses , too. So, when the news dropped about the show's renewal, I should have known Bond’s announcement was on deck.

Interestingly, despite the announcements coming almost at the same time, there are also rumors that Lowden might not be part of Seasons 9 and 10. A report in Variety calls Lowden’s return “uncertain.” I’m not sure what to make of that. The book-to-screen adaptation has been adapting one book per season, generally. Season 6 was an exception, as it combined two books , the 6th and 7th in Mick Herron’s series Slough House. That's not all, though.

articles.title: 5 Unexpected Deaths in the Absolute Universe That Shook Us to Our Very Cores
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics DC Comics’ Absolute Universe has been the highlight of the comic book industry for the past two years. Its gripping reimaginings of classic DC heroes as underdogs fighting institutional injustice have been a total success. But as expected in a darker, twisted universe, many versions of iconic characters are at risk of dying. Indeed, without […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google DC Comics ’ Absolute Universe has been the highlight of the comic book industry for the past two years. Its gripping reimaginings of classic DC heroes as underdogs fighting institutional injustice have been a total success. But as expected in a darker, twisted universe, many versions of iconic characters are at risk of dying. Indeed, without the restraints of the main DC Universe’s status quo, the Absolute Universe has delivered some truly shocking deaths of our favorite characters. These deaths proved that the Absolute Universe would be unlike anything we’ve seen before and that no one is safe from Darkseid’s cruel meddling.

In a world dominated by villains, the heroes have to be extra careful to keep their loved ones safe. If the heroes fail, the villains won’t hesitate to strike.

In the main DC Universe, Commissioner Jim Gordon is one of Batman’s most trusted allies and an ever-present source of support within the GCPD. A similar closeness exists in the Absolute Universe, as former commissioner and mayor Gordon was, in many ways, a father figure to a young Bruce after Thomas's death. This version of Gordon even figured out that Bruce is Batman. But that wasn’t all Gordon discovered; he found files linking the Joker and Scarecrow to Bruce’s origin. When Gordon went to tell Batman, Scarecrow used his gas to manipulate the former mayor into jumping off the roof. Even though Batman tried to save Gordon, he was too late, and Gordon fell to his death . Scarecrow used Gordon’s death to frame Batman for murder and make him public enemy number one. Gordon has always been the moral center of Gotham and its police department, and his death in the Absolute Universe showed how the city was now fully under the Joker’s control.

One of the driving aspects of Absolute Superman was that once he arrived on Earth, he had no human family and was homeless. However, when Superman first crash-landed in Kansas, the farmers Jon and Martha Kent took him in. The kind-hearted couple treated Superman like their own son and were poised to have a happy life together. However, it all came crashing down when Lazarus Corps and the Peacemakers arrived to capture Superman. The Kents told Superman to run and save himself, which the teenager tearfully obliged. Superman would force himself to stay away from the Kents for years to keep them safe from Ra’s al Ghul’s minions. Over time, Jon would die, and Martha’s mind would begin to deteriorate with age. Eventually, Martha would pass away as well, but not before leaving Superman two presents: a homemade costume and the name Clark Kent. Even if the Kents didn’t spend much time with Superman, they still convinced the Kryptonian that there’s beauty in humanity.

The Absolute Universe turned the Robins from Batman’s greatest allies to some of his most powerful enemies. Dick Grayson, Jason Todd, Tim Drake, Stephanie Brown, and Duke Thomas were all brought into the Robin program to hunt down and terminate Batman for supposedly killing Jim Gordon. This leads to Jason and Tim apprehending Batman and preparing to arrest him. However, as the two Robins celebrate, Clayface emerges. With Jason working for the Joker, one would assume the Boy Wonder’s fate was sealed. However, in a complete subversion of expectations, Clayface disguises himself as Batman and kills Tim instead . This tragic death causes Batman to be framed for another murderer and for Jason to swear vengeance against the Caped Crusader. So, within a single storyline, the Joker and his goons took away two of Batman’s most iconic allies. Not only that, but Jason is now poised to become one of the Dark Knight’s most hateful enemies.

When Wally West was announced as the Absolute Flash, the first question on everyone’s mind was what had happened to the last Scarlet Speedster, Barry Allen. The answer is that Barry died so Wally could get his powers. While Barry was working on an experiment to create a portal to the Speed Force, Wally was caught in it and turned into a being of pure energy. Barry grabbed onto Wally and tried to help the teenager ground himself and revert to his physical form. However, in his panicked state, Wally accidentally shot Barry with a lightning bolt before running as fast as he could. Even worse, Barry was still holding onto Wally, so he was dragged for miles, and the immense speed tore off all the flesh from his body. Overcome with guilt for accidentally killing his mentor, Wally would don Barry’s suit to become the Flash. However, while Barry’s body died, his soul became tethered to the Still Point dimension, serving as a ghostly ally to Wally.

After DC Comics announced the Absolute Green Arrow miniseries, fans everywhere were shocked and horrified by the supposed first appearance of the Emerald Archer. In the Absolute Evil one-shot, Oliver Queen’s first appearance shows him training in his Arrowcave and preparing to use his archery skills to take down cruel billionaires like Jubal Slade. However, Queen’s plans come to a sudden and gruesome end when Hawkman, under the orders of Veronica Cale, brutally murdered the would-be Green Arrow. That death immediately got everybody talking about who or what Absolute Green Arrow was. Until the very end, people theorized about how Oliver could have possibly come back to life . But all those theories were proven to be false when Absolute Green Arrow was revealed to be Malcom Merlyn and Connor Hawke. Oliver’s death shocked everyone and became the driving force behind the Absolute Green Arrow series. The Green Arrow mantle has always been intrinsically tied to Oliver, but his death showed that his legacy and mission could live on through others.

Who else do you think is going to die in the Absolute Universe? Leave a Comment below and join the conversation in the ComicBook Forum!

Angad Aulakh ’s lifelong fascination with space inspired Aurora, a sci-fi short about an astronaut left stranded after a mission goes catastrophically wrong. Freddie Ballard ( Guy Kent ) is sent to investigate a mysterious signal, but an accident makes him the sole survivor, with no way home and growing doubts about what his superiors have told him.

Shot in black and white, the film draws on German Expressionism and retro-futurism to create its unique visual world. Aulakh and Kent talk to Deadline about shaping Freddie’s journey, building the film’s cosmic scale on a short-film budget and their plans for what lies beyond the vast reaches of the galaxy they created. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Actor Russell Tovey Dismantles The Manosphere In His Award-Winning Performance In 'I Am The Prize' News 'Vultures' Swoops To Top Award At Oscar-Qualifying HollyShorts Film Festival: Winners List

ANGAD AULAKH: It really started with a lifelong obsession with space and the idea that we are not alone in the universe. It’s one of the most compelling ideas for storytellers and people in general. When we look at how short our lives are, how small Earth is and how vast the universe is, the possibilities for what’s out there are so exciting. It’s the idea that we might not even be asking the right questions yet. We don’t know which questions to ask because there are concepts so grand and profound. Exploring them through storytelling felt like a wonderful opportunity.

With short films, you have more leeway to be a little avant-garde. I often liken short films to haikus, while features are full-fledged novels. So I wanted to focus on the emotion, the moment, the visuals and the wonder of space. Technology has evolved so much that it’s why we can make a film like this on our budget today.

I’m happy to say we didn’t use any AI on the film. I’m not throwing shade at AI, by any means, but I know it’s a big part of the conversation right now. It started with looking up at the stars and wondering what’s out there and what stories I could explore in the vastness of space.

GUY KENT: I was thrilled because I also have a lifelong fascination with space and our place in [the cosmos]. As Angad said, we have so many questions and no answers. Finding some faith that there’s meaning despite not having the answers is profound to me. When this idea came up, it was an exciting adventure to embark on.

Angad and I have been deliberate about budget and scope, especially with short films. We prioritize quality and want to understand what we can and can’t achieve. With this film, the next question was, “How are we going to pull this off? How do we make it feel like the work we want to do, while making sure it works, resonates and lets the emotional moments land?”

Our pre-production work and the team we’ve worked with in the past gave us a built-in shorthand. That was especially true with our cinematographer, but finding a stage where we could create a set and build on it was also a huge part of making this feasible.

DEADLINE: The short film rests on you, Guy. You have a lot of scenes on your own. Your character is not only lost in space, but lost to himself, or somewhere in between. How did the two of you work on that story? What would you like audiences to think about through that juxtaposition?

KENT: Angad and I had a lot of discussions that began with isolation. Isolation isn’t something you show; it’s something you sit in. It’s revealing to see what happens when all distractions are removed and there’s no barrier between you and your own thoughts.

For Freddie, there’s a chance to find himself again. He’s an astronaut trained for crisis, someone who understands how to solve most of the problems he faces. Here, he’s confronted with something very personal and existential that he has no answers for.

It would be interesting if audiences were left wondering not only how they would react to meeting something beyond Earth, but also considering the hope that there’s something greater. As Angad said, even if we don’t have answers to these questions, there can be meaning in an unknowable answer. That makes you feel found in a way.

DEADLINE: Angad, what was the hardest thing about putting this story together?

AULAKH: The biggest challenge was looking at short films as a whole and thinking about how much time we had and how long the film would be. There are practical considerations, too. A lot of festivals won’t accept a short film longer than 15 minutes.

AULAKH: There are practical considerations around the film’s life after it’s released, but audiences also expect a short film to be short. Ideally, you’re not making a 30- or 40-minute short, because then you might as well make a feature. We had to think about the real estate available to us and the most effective way to make audiences leave having felt something and gone on an emotional experience. That’s what I’m interested in as a filmmaker: moving people. A big part of that is considering how the music, sound design, performance and production design work together to convey something cinematic and effective.

You also want to tell a compelling story. Weaving Freddie’s journey into a cohesive narrative in 15 minutes was always going to be a challenge, but I’m pleased with how it turned out. We focused on the emotion and on the fact that a mission has gone wrong. This astronaut is either going to be killed aboard the spacecraft or find his way home. I hoped the quieter moments would sustain the audience because they’d want to stick around to see whether Freddie makes it. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

DEADLINE: Let’s talk about the scope of the film. The cinematography is great. Why black and white as your color scheme?

AULAKH: German Expressionism was on my mind as I wrote the screenplay and thought about the aesthetic I wanted. The other reason is that we don’t see many black-and-white films set in space or black-and-white science-fiction films. More than anything, I think it looks gorgeous on screen. The light on the set, shining through the top grates, was beautiful.

We had scouted locations beforehand, so we knew what the set would look like. But the first image that came to mind was Freddie Ballard lying on the floor, screaming and tumbling. I saw it in black and white. I hadn’t shot a black-and-white film since film school, and I thought this was the perfect opportunity. The stars look beautiful in black and white. There was also a practical reason. Black and white is more forgiving when you don’t have a huge budget for production design. You can hide things in the shadows, and it worked well with our special effects and the 3D modeling. We also made sequences in Unreal Engine with Stuart Lippincott, who’s an absolute genius. His work was a huge inspiration to me. I thought the lighting, images, and compositions would be tremendous in black and white.

KENT: On an emotional level, I think black and white subconsciously creates a sense of melancholy. That’s the basis of German Expressionism, at least in my experience. There’s an emotional texture it brings.

AULAKH: Yeah, it’s very melancholic. Black and white also has inherent cinematic associations. Audiences think of films from the 1930s and ’40s, most of which were made in black and white. I love the idea that Aurora can feel like a product of the past, something you might have seen in those bygone eras. That was exciting because retro-futurism, which is used extensively in science-fiction films and video games, is powerful and interesting. I gravitate toward it, so I loved being able to use that aesthetic in Aurora .

DEADLINE: What were the biggest technical challenges, and where did you have to get especially inventive? You’ve talked about using black and white, but is there another example? How did you get inventive with the production design?

AULAKH: A lot of the credit goes to our visual effects artist, Ian Mills Miller. The entity you see in the film was originally going to be an actor, Ethan [Daniel Corbett], wearing a latex bodysuit. We were going to use his movements and digitally map them onto a being, the way they did with Gollum in The Lord of the Rings . Instead, we used Ethan as a reference, and Ian created the magnificent 3D being you see in the film.

That’s a hard shot to pull off because it’s expensive and time-consuming, and you have to be careful about how much you show. Black and white allowed us to hide the entity in the shadows. He’s a being of light at the end of the film, but throughout it he looks dark and mechanical. He’s influenced more by machinery than by alien life.

It was tricky. Having the ability to hide him in the shadows and take a less-is-more approach was effective. If you hold an effects shot too long, the audience may start to look at it differently. Even in major motion pictures, it can be disconcerting and create an uncanny valley effect. We wanted to avoid that with our digital effects.

DEADLINE: Talk a bit about your experience on the film festival circuit. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

AULAKH: I’ll take the first part, and Guy can talk about where we’ve been and what’s coming up. We premiered at HollyShorts this August, which was a lovely experience. I’m a small-town kid from Mountaintop, Pennsylvania. We didn’t have a movie theater in town, and we still don’t. Getting to screen a film at the historic Grauman's Chinese Theatre was an honor.

The festival was so well put together, and the audience response was wonderful. There were events throughout the week, so you had a chance to meet other filmmakers and talk with people watching your film. As a filmmaker, you get real-time feedback from the room. Unfortunately, we can’t attend many festivals because they’re all over the world. The few opportunities we get to sit with an audience and see the film on the big screen are phenomenal. It’s been wonderful so far. Our last few shorts had great festival runs, and we hope Aurora will top both of them. We’re just getting started. Guy can tell you more about where we’re headed next.

KENT: We’re going to FilmQuest. We are nominated for Best Sci-Fi Short and Best Visual Effects, which is fantastic. We’re thrilled to be part of that festival and what it represents. They’ve been wonderful. We’ve also done Anomaly Film Festival and Toronto Arthouse, and we’re going to Festival of Fantastic Films in the U.K. We have some other festivals to be announced toward the end of the year and early next year.

The greatest thing, as Angad said, is connecting with audiences and getting the film’s message out there. I think it’s a special piece, and there’s more to this world that we hope to build beyond the short. The more audiences see it, the more we’ll be able to go down that road.

AULAKH: We’re developing a television series based on Aurora and its world. If we can build some excitement throughout the festival circuit, it’ll make getting the series off the ground that much easier. We hope people respond to the film. After the festival circuit, we’ll release it online; we’re working on distribution for that, too.

These festival runs can last upwards of a year and a half, if you’re lucky. We’re excited to get the film out there around the world, and it has officially gone international. Sometimes things can go right in life, and this is luckily one of those situations. I don’t want to knock on wood as I say that. We’re thrilled and honored to be selected.

articles.title: Stephen Colbert Signs With UTA
articles.summary: The former ‘Late Show’ host and current ‘Lord of the Rings’ writer will be represented by the Beverly Hills-based talent agency.
articles.content:
Stephen Colbert has signed with UTA as he explores opportunities after The Late Show concluded earlier this year, The Hollywood Reporter has learned.

UTA will be representing the 13-time Emmy winner as well as his production company, Spartina Industries, across film, television, publishing work and more.

"We are thrilled to be working with Stephen Colbert. He is an exceptionally talented artist and creator, a dedicated philanthropist and a terrific person,” UTA president of filmed entertainment Matt Rice and managing partners Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan said in a joint statement. “We look forward to partnering with Stephen and Spartina Industries to support and further expand his creative endeavors."

Colbert signed off from The Late Show in May after hosting the late-night series, which became a casualty of the Paramount-Skydance merger , for a decade. In the process, the comedian — who also wrote on and executive produced the series — collected several of his many Emmys as well as a Peabody Award.

Prior to his tenure at The Late Show , Colbert hosted, wrote and produced Comedy Central’s satire news program The Colbert Report for nine years and wrote and served as a correspondent on The Daily Show for seven years.

And Colbert is keeping busy post- Late Show . Currently, he’s co-writing the next Lord of the Rings movie with veteran LOTR screenwriter Philippa Boyens and his son Peter McGee, as well as working on his screenwriting software company Scripto. In a recent interview with THR , Colbert said he has been entertaining other opportunities but hasn’t landed on one yet. “There’s some fun stuff to think about. I’m in no hurry,” he said.

His production company, Spartina Industries, is currently developing a TV adaptation of Roger Zelazny’s sci-fi book series The Chronicles of Amber with The Walking Dead co-creator Robert Kirkman’s Skybound Entertainment. The company, headed up by Carrie Byalick, previously produced two seasons of the late-night show After Midnight on CBS.

Colbert continues to be managed by James Baby Doll Dixon at Dixon Talent, Inc. and represented by Tom Hansen and Don Steele at Hansen, Jacobson, Teller, Hoberman.

articles.title: 'Birthright,' About Differing Attitudes on Israel, Set For Broadway
articles.summary: The play follows seven friends through 18 years, starting just after their Birthright trip to Israel.
articles.content:
Birthright, a play by Tony Award winner Jonathan Spector examining differing views about Israel among Jewish-American friends, will move to Broadway this spring.

The play is set for a 20-week run at Broadway’s Hudson Theatre starting Feb. 23, 2027, ahead of a March 15 opening night. It moves to Broadway after a sold-out and critically acclaimed run at the Off-Broadway MCC Theater this past summer. Teddy Bergman directs, making his Broadway debut after helming the Off-Broadway run.

Casting for the Broadway run has not yet been announced.

The play follows seven friends through 18 years, starting just after their Birthright trip to Israel in 2006, tracking their differing and changing attitudes on Israel as well as changes within their own lives. Spector returns to Broadway after last season’s Eureka Day, which won the Tony Award for best revival of a play, and centered on a school board dealing with select parents who did not want to vaccinate their kids.

“Just over two years ago, I was racing to finish a first draft of Birthright before starting rehearsals for Eureka Day at MTC. I could never have fathomed that such a short time later we’d be bringing it to Broadway, when the questions the play is wrestling with still feel so close to our present moment. Writing this was the scariest thing I’ve ever attempted to do, and (perhaps not coincidentally), has become the most meaningful and rewarding. I’m beyond thrilled that a wider audience will have a chance to encounter the play and see the work of our brilliant artistic collaborators,” Spector said.

articles.title: Afterlife With Archie TV Show Confirms Riverdale Replacement Cast for Disney+ Horror Series
articles.summary: Disney+ has confirmed the cast for the Afterlife With Archie TV series, and it means the R-Rated comic adaptation is getting even closer to reality. After seven seasons of Riverdale on The CW and four seasons of The Chilling Adventures of Sabrina on Netflix, fans may have thought that the modern TV takes on Archie […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Disney+ has confirmed the cast for the Afterlife With Archie TV series, and it means the R-Rated comic adaptation is getting even closer to reality. After seven seasons of Riverdale on The CW and four seasons of The Chilling Adventures of Sabrina on Netflix, fans may have thought that the modern TV takes on Archie had hit their ceiling. Despite this, Disney, of all places, confirmed that the horror-themed comic series Afterlife With Archie had been given a series order on Disney+ , and now the new versions of the main cast have been confirmed.

In a new report on Deadline , the casting for Afterlife With Archie has been confirmed, with a slew of newcomers taking on the parts. Vasco Faria of Your Fault: London will take on the titular role of Archie, now caught between the life-and-death stakes of a zombie invasion and navigating the choice between Betty and Veronica. Sarah Abbott ( The Body ) and Aliyah Mastin ( Paradise ) will take on those respective roles from the pages of Archie comics, with Angel Rivera ( Escape from Mr. Lemoncello’s Library ) confirmed as the new Jughead Jones; and Chloe Avakian ( Devil in Disguise: John Wayne Gacy ) as the new Sabrina Spellman.

Meet Riverdale's newest residents. #AfterlifewithArchie pic.twitter.com/RRZ2m3Msab

The new Afterlife With Archie TV series is in good hands from the jump, with creator Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa bringing it to life in live-action. Previously, not only did Aguirre-Sacasa help shepherd the characters back to prominence with both Riverdale and Chilling Adventures of Sabrina , but he also penned the original Afterlife With Archie comic book series .

It could be argued that the Afterlife With Archie comics, which put a grim horror lens on top of the ever-pleasant Riverdale setting, is what helped revive the idea of the characters in mainstream pop culture. Not only were the comics really popular, but it ended up being what gave Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa the keys to the kingdom, acting as chief creative officer for Archie Comics.

The most surprising thing about Disney+ being the home for a live-action Afterlife With Archie TV series is twofold: the first being that the source material does not shy away from grim violence in the slightest. Recent years have shown that Disney is less squimish about mature material being on the streaming platform than when it first launched, but Afterlife With Archie isn't shy on gory details. As for the second, comic readers will know well that the series itself simply stopped, ending on a cliffhanger, with no new issues released since Issue #10 arrived over a decade ago.

In that regard, the good news for comic readers is that the Afterlife With Archie TV series may well adapt all of the released material quite quickly, propelling the story beyond what was published and finally offering some closure for a story that appeared to be abandoned. That said, it's still a major question mark about how gross this show can really get when it will be advertised alongside the likes of Mickey Mouse Clubhouse and even Percy Jackson . At the very least, a live-action recreation of the comic's iconic zombie Jughead image will be striking promotional material one day.

articles.title: Jimmy Kimmel Had More Trump Jokes, But I Didn’t See The CMAs Jokes Coming
articles.summary: Sorry to anyone named Luke.
articles.content:
If you’ve been watching Jimmy Kimmel Live ! – or if not live on social media – you should know commentary on President Trump and the White House in general has become an almost nightly occurrence. There’s a lot of history behind the contention, from Kimmel’s pointed jokes , to Trump and the White House’s bold insults , and FCC involvement in between. So, a Trump segment on late night? Not unexpected. Random shots thrown at the CMAs? A bit more surprising.

Last night Kimmel did spend a fair chunk of his monologue focusing on President Trump and Trump's recent visit to China. Though he made some comments about Communism, the weirdest thing he noticed about the visit was that the President seems to be wearing makeup on his hands these days to give him a little more youthful vigor.

The Trump bit went on for a while in more traditional Jimmy Kimmel Live! style, and we'll have to wait and see if the President responds . Still, I was more amused this week by Kimmel trying to get in on the CMAs commentary. Let's get into the bobsledding joke, shall we?

OK, maybe I shouldn’t have been as surprised as I was to see Kimmel commenting on country music given the CMAs aired on ABC with a big, splashy Taylor Swift appearance (that led to some Swiftie theories ). That's his own network, and it's nice to see him playing ball, even if some rumors have called his relationship with the network "unmanageable. "

That last bit is a Willie Nelson joke, which is quite funny, but only if you already know the Lifetime Achievement Award is named for him. I did not see it coming though when Kimmel brought up bobsledding in regards to “Choosin' Texas.”

Yeah, that’s a joke, but it’s also just the kind of absurd fact that’s worth remarking on. Ella Langley's crushing it, and this milestone is cool, but now I'll never think of it without also thinking of Olympics bobsledding . Sure, these are some fairly light jokes compared to his Trump stuff, but please don't say Mr. Kimmel never did anything for pop culture.

articles.title: Imax Inks Largest Cinema Deal In U.K. For New Locations
articles.summary: The agreement for U.K. and European theater locations with Moshe “Mooky” Greidinger's Showcase Cinemas gets Imax back in business with the former Cineworld Group CEO.
articles.content:
Imax is back in business with former Cineworld Group CEO Moshe “Mooky” Greidinger after signing a deal for 13 new laser projection systems at 12 theaters in the Showcase Cinemas circuit in the U.K. and Europe.

Terms of the agreement were not disclosed, but Imax has signed its first deal with Showcase Cinemas, but also with a longtime business partner. “I’ve been in the Imax business for decades and the value of its technology, brand, and strategic partnership to exhibitors have grown exponentially in that time,” Greidinger said in a statement after his recent acquisition of the 16-venue Showcase Cinemas circuit from Skydance.

“There is no doubt that Imax plays a significant role in the results of the industry and I am sure it will continue to grow and attract new audience and become even more significant in the coming years. I look forward to working with Rich and his team and making the Imax Experience a cornerstone of the new Showcase Cinemas in the UK,” he added.

The new laser projection systems will go in 12 UK locations and another in Europe. Regal owner Cineworld in 2023 emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceeding in the U.S. via a restructuring, with Greidinger and his management team eventually leaving the British cinema operator.

“Mooky is a visionary leader and an excellent partner who recognized the value in Imax long before our recent run of record-breaking success. We’re excited to be back in business with his team at Showcase Cinemas UK,” Richard Gelfond, CEO of Imax, said in his own statement.

Five of the new Imax locations will open across the UK in 2027, with the remaining locations to open in the next few years, Imax said. The deal also comes as Imax shows momentum in new theater signings after the release of Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey on its screens, and ahead of the debut of Dune: Part Three at Imax locations worldwide.

The deal announcement with Showcase Cinemas also comes a day after Imax said it had promoted Giovanni Dolci to the newly created role of chief operating officer, overseeing the company’s expanding global theater network.

articles.title: John Carpenter Confirms Involvement in Zack Snyder's Escape From New York Reboot, And in the Perfect Role
articles.summary: John Carpenter's '80s cult-classic sci-fi action film Escape From New York is getting a remake from Watchmen and Batman v Superman director Zack Snyder. Snyder is doing a re-imagining of the original film's concept, moving the timeline further ahead to the 1990s (as opposed to the '80s), with some whole new subtext about the dystopian […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google John Carpenter's '80s cult-classic sci-fi action film Escape From New York is getting a remake from Watchmen and Batman v Superman director Zack Snyder. Snyder is doing a re-imagining of the original film's concept , moving the timeline further ahead to the 1990s (as opposed to the '80s), with some whole new subtext about the dystopian version of America where New York City has been transformed into a penal colony.

In addition to teasing bits and pieces of Escape From New York 's story, Snyder has also hinted that John Carpenter is invovled with the film. Today, we're getting confirmation that Carpenter is not just invovled with Escape From New York in an advisory role, but is actually part of the crew of the film – in a perfect job slot.

John Carpenter was on Star Trek: The Next Generation alumni Brent Spiner and Jonathan Frakes' podcast Dropping Names , and the subject of Snyder's Escape from New York remake came up – specifically the film's score. John Carpenter made his mark on cinema with films like Halloween (1978), Escape from New York (1981), and The Thing (1982), not just because of his indie directing and creative bends on genre, but also because of the iconic scores for those films, two of which ( Halloween and EfNY ) Carpenter composed himself. So the question is: Who is composing Zack Snyder's Escape from New York ?

The answer: John Carpenter is. As the filmmaker told Spiner and Frakes (quite frankly): “I demanded to be the composer … and they’re not going to use my score, we’re going to remake the score.”

As stated, Escape from New York was one of Carpenter's earliest achievements as both a director and a composer, and proof that Halloween was no fluke. Having Carpenter back to compose the score instantly lends credibility to Snyder's remake, which is something the project definitely needs. Snyder's reputation has taken a hit after a string of frustrating projects launched through his Netflix deal. That includes the franchise non-starter Army of the Dead and a failed attempt to launch a new Star Wars-style franchise with Rebel Moon. In fact, Escape from New York has some fans on board precisely because it brings Snyder back to a grounded place: re-envisioning someone else's work , which has produced his most acclaimed films ( Dawn of the Dead, 300, Watchmen ).

With Carpenter there, literally watching every frame of the film as he composes for it, you can rest assured that Snyder will be collaborating a lot more on this film than he usually does.

Escape from New York is currently in production. No release date has been set.
